title.narrative: Advancing global maritime decarbonization through financing sustainable maritime transport

description.narrative: Acceleration of financial investments in maritime decarbonization in developing countries (with a focus on SIDS and LDCs), which is expected to lead to future reductions in GHG emissions, a healthier and more sustainable marine environment, and socio-economic benefits such as job creation and improved access to clean energy.
Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

The project will deliver a range of socioeconomic benefits at both national and local levels, particularly in developing countries, including SIDS and LDCs. These benefits are closely linked to the project's overarching goal of accelerating financial investments in maritime decarbonization in developing countries and contribute directly to the achievement of global environmental benefits under the GEF Trust Fund. At the national and local levels, the project will: · Create quality jobs in emerging sectors such as renewable energy, port infrastructure development, and alternative fuel supply chains. The maritime energy transition is expected to generate approximately four million jobs globally, with a significant share in developing countries. · Strengthen institutional capacity by equipping national authorities, port operators, and financial institutions with the tools and knowledge needed to develop and implement bankable decarbonization projects. · Improve access to clean energy by catalyzing investments in renewable energy generation and infrastructure, which are essential for producing alternative marine fuels. · Promote gender equity by addressing persistent gender imbalances in the maritime and energy sectors, ensuring inclusive participation in training, decision-making, and employment opportunities. · Enhance regional cooperation and South-South learning, enabling countries to share best practices and adapt successful financing models to their own contexts. These socioeconomic benefits translate into global environmental benefits by: · Enabling deep reductions in GHG emissions from the maritime sector, which currently accounts for nearly 3% of global emissions. · Supporting the transition to alternative fuels and technologies, which are essential for meeting the IMO’s climate targets. · Strengthening the resilience of supply chains and port operations, contributing to healthier marine ecosystems and reduced pollution. · Unlocking private and domestic capital for climate mitigation, thereby addressing market failures and accelerating the global energy transition. Direct beneficiaries of the project include: · National governments and maritime authorities in developing countries. · Port operators and infrastructure developers. · Local and regional financial institutions. · Technical partners and private sector actors engaged in clean energy and maritime transport. · Women and underrepresented groups in the maritime and energy sectors. By addressing systemic barriers and enabling inclusive, sustainable investment, the project ensures that developing countries can actively participate in and benefit from the global maritime energy transition, while contributing meaningfully to climate mitigation and sustainable development goals.
